title: Fixation and Dehydration Protocol for Scanning Electron Microscopy
author: Mario A. Sandoval-Molina
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k3vcyn6

steps.title: Prepare phosphate buffer (0.1 M, pH 7.2)
steps.instruction: Make two 0.2 M stock solutions in deionised water, then combine them to obtain 200 mL of 0.1 M phosphate buffer at pH 7.2.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve NaH2PO4·H2O (Sigma‑Aldrich S3139, BioUltra, ≥99.0%) in deionised water to a final concentration of 0.2 M (stock solution A).
Dissolve Na2HPO4·7H2O (Sigma‑Aldrich S7907, Ultra, ≥99.5%) in deionised water to a final concentration of 0.2 M (stock solution B).
Mix 28 mL of stock A, 72 mL of stock B and 100 mL deionised water in a clean container to give 200 mL of 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.2).
If necessary, adjust the pH to 7.2 with 1 N HCl or 5 M NaOH.

steps.title: Prepare 10 % glutaraldehyde fixation solution
steps.instruction: Combine 10 mL of 25 % glutaraldehyde (electron‑microscopy grade, Merck, Germany) with 90 mL of the 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.2) to make 100 mL of a 10 % glutaraldehyde fixative.

steps.title: Prepare 1 % osmium tetroxide solution
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, dissolve 0.25 g of OsO4 in 25 mL deionised water, protect the solution from light and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Critical‑point dry samples
steps.instruction: Place the fixed samples in a Samdri‑780 critical‑point dryer (Tousim Research Corporation, Rockville, USA) and run the drying cycle according to the instrument’s standard protocol.

steps.title: Mount and double‑coat samples
steps.instruction: Mount each dried sample on a copper stud using carbon conductive tape, then apply a double coating supplied by Ted Pella I.N.C. (USA).

steps.title: Sputter‑coat with gold‑palladium
steps.instruction: Sputter‑coat the double‑coated samples with a gold‑palladium alloy using a Fine‑Coat ion sputter (JFC‑1100, JEOL Ltd., Tokyo, Japan).

steps.title: Observe samples by SEM
steps.instruction: Image the coated specimens on a JEOL JSM‑6390 scanning electron microscope operated at 25 kV.
